observation: Whole set in the opening position on the repaired build, all three views inspected. TOP: the 7x9 field is complete and mirror-symmetric -- a den flanked by three traps at each end, the twelve asteroid-belt tiles as two 2x3 blocks either side of the centre file, and sixteen worlds each centred on its own cell, eight on white discs and eight on black. No piece straddles a cell boundary, no tile sits proud of its pocket, both storage trays clear of the board. FRONT: every disc is fully landed on the board top, the size ladder reads correctly with Jupiter the largest globe and Mars and Earth the smallest, Saturn's ring is a near-level brim and Uranus's an upright hoop, and the two corona flame cones rise from their own tiles and touch nothing. ISO: no floating geometry, no part passing through another, no missing or duplicated piece; nothing has moved since the previous assembled round on any world but Neptune. The two Neptune globes carry their three white bands, the dark spot and the companion oval; at whole-set framing the companion is at the limit of what the frame resolves, which is expected for a 1.9 x 1.0 mm marking on a 21.9 mm globe and is why the per-world frames carry it. The assembly package holds 222 occurrences, two more than the published set, and the two are exactly the companion bodies. Every one of the 24 components was rebuilt and matched its recorded isolated pass, so all 24 print verdicts are carried on unchanged geometry.
